worker_target_description: Study 1, Great Value peanut-butter price-magnitude evaluations: interaction of left-digit difference ($4.01 versus $3.00; $4.00 versus $2.99) and stimulus-based simultaneous versus memory-based sequential presentation, in the two-way between-subjects ANOVA.
worker_notes: Only es_value_o is assigned; all other value fields are unassigned placeholders. Both assigned descriptions explicitly identify the same original Study 1 factorial interaction, irrespective of the different replication labels. Table 2 prints partial eta-squared .033, not standardized beta; metric identity was checked on rendered PDF page 7. Study 1 Results (p. 776) reports the same interaction F(1, 141) = 4.84, p = .029; simple contrasts are distinct tests (stimulus-based F = 8.08; memory-based F = .08) and were not substituted. No effect-size conversion or N derivation performed.

coding_context.description: In this paper, the authors offer insight into a previously documented observation known as the left-digit bias, whereby consumers tend to give greater weight to the left-most digit when comparing two prices. This means, for example, that consumers tend to treat a price difference of $4.00 vs. $2.99 as larger than $4.01 vs. $3.00. The authors’ key claim is that this bias is greater when the prices are presented side-by-side, in a way that makes them easier to compare, than sequentially, on two separate but consecutive screens.
coding_context.reported_success_quote: We find marginally significant support for the authors’ key interaction in both replications. [...] Although the evidence is much weaker than in the original study, we are inclined to believe that the original effect is real.

parent_response: New separately authorised source-grouped completion. Fresh blind extraction and exact evidence now supplied. Reconcile prior findings/holds explicitly; numeric agreement alone is not target identification. Do not infer unknown sample roles or individual author verdicts from a shared paper-level label.
